html:
The Ukrainian People's Republic was a Ukrainian state proclaimed in Kyiv on 20 November 1917 by the Central Rada, a council led by the historian Mykhailo Hrushevsky, after the Russian Revolution. It declared full independence in January 1918.

It fought the Bolsheviks for Kyiv, which changed hands many times. In early 1918 it signed a peace with Germany at Brest-Litovsk, and German troops replaced it with the Hetmanate of Pavlo Skoropadsky. Restored under Symon Petliura, it united on paper with the West Ukrainian republic in January 1919, but lost to the Red Army, White armies and Poland. Pogroms by various forces killed tens of thousands of Jews. By 1921 the Bolsheviks held most of Ukraine. Its blue and yellow flag and trident returned in 1991 with the independence of Ukraine.
